# Is 1200 a Good SAT Score? 2026 Percentiles & Colleges


## **TL;DR**


Yes, a 1200 SAT score is a good score overall. It puts you well above the average SAT score and around the upper portion of the test-taking population. A 1200 is competitive at many public universities and can qualify students for merit scholarships at some colleges. However, it is below the typical range at highly selective universities. Whether you should submit, retake, or stop depends on your target colleges, GPA, intended major, and scholarship goals.


---


A 1200 on the SAT is a good score. It sits about 170 points above the national average of 1029 (based on College Board data for the Class of 2025), and it puts you ahead of roughly 74% to 76% of everyone who took the test. That’s a strong position.


But you probably already sense the follow-up question: good for what? A 1200 is more than enough for hundreds of solid universities. It falls short for the most selective schools. And it sits right at the threshold where merit scholarships start to appear. The rest of this guide breaks down exactly what a 1200 means for your college list, your wallet, and your next move.


If you’re still figuring out where your score might land, try the[SAT score predictor](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/score-predictors) to see how your section scores project.


> **Quick Answer: Is 1200 a Good SAT Score?**
>
>
> Yes, a 1200 SAT score is good for many college applicants. It is well above the national average and places you ahead of most SAT test-takers. A 1200 can make you competitive at hundreds of colleges and may qualify you for merit scholarships at some universities. However, it is below the typical range at highly selective schools, so whether you should submit or retake depends on your target colleges.

## What Does a 1200 SAT Score Mean in 2026?


The SAT runs on a 400 to 1600 scale. It has two sections, Reading & Writing and Math, each scored from 200 to 800. Your two section scores are added together for the composite.


A 1200 composite means you’re performing well above average. The national average for the Class of 2025 was 1029 (521 Reading & Writing, 508 Math), so a 1200 represents a meaningful gap.


One thing most articles skip: there are actually two percentile numbers for every SAT score. Among students who actually took the SAT (the “User” percentile), a 1200 lands around the 74th to 76th percentile. But the College Board also calculates a “Nationally Representative” percentile that estimates where you’d fall among all U.S. students, not just test-takers. By that measure, a 1200 is around the 81st percentile. The difference exists because the pool of SAT takers skews more college-bound than the general high school population. For a deeper explanation of why these numbers differ, see our guide on[SAT percentiles](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/sat-percentiles-user-vs-national-guide) .


### How Strong Is a 1200 SAT Score?


A 1200 is best described as a **good SAT score, but not a highly selective score** .


It is strong enough to make you a viable applicant at many public universities and regional universities. It can also become more valuable when paired with a strong GPA, rigorous coursework, meaningful extracurricular activities, and a college list that includes schools where your score falls within or above the middle 50% SAT range.


The important distinction is between being a good score nationally and being a good score for a particular college.


A 1200 can be excellent for one university, average for another, and well below the typical admitted-student range at a highly selective school.

A stronger Math score can be particularly useful for engineering, computer science, mathematics, and other quantitative programs, while a stronger Reading & Writing score may be more relevant to some humanities and social-science programs.


However, colleges generally evaluate your complete academic profile rather than using a single SAT section in isolation.


## What Percentile Is a 1200 SAT Score?


A 1200 SAT score has two commonly referenced percentile rankings in College Board reporting:


-


**SAT User Percentile:** Compares your score with students in the SAT score-reporting population.


-


**Nationally Representative Percentile:** Estimates how your score compares with all U.S. students in the relevant grade, including students who did not take the SAT.


These numbers can differ substantially because SAT test-takers are not a random sample of all U.S. students. The exact percentile can also change when College Board updates its reference population.


For that reason, use the current College Board percentile table when publishing the exact 2026 percentile rather than treating an older percentile as permanent.


### Why Percentile Matters


Percentile tells you how your score compares with other students. It does **not** tell you your probability of admission to a particular college.


For admissions decisions, a college's current SAT range is usually more useful than your national percentile.


For example, a 1200 may put you well above the average SAT test-taker while still being below the typical range at a highly selective university.

## Can You Get Scholarships With a 1200 SAT Score?


Yes. A 1200 SAT score can qualify students for merit scholarships at some colleges, although the exact award depends on the university, GPA, residency, enrollment status, application date, and other eligibility requirements.


Some universities use automatic merit grids that award money based on combinations of SAT/ACT scores and GPA. Others use competitive scholarships that require a separate application.

### Why Increasing From 1200 to 1300 Can Matter


Merit scholarships often use score thresholds. A student who is just below a published threshold may receive a substantially different award after crossing it.


For that reason, if a target college offers a larger scholarship at 1250, 1300, or 1350, retaking the SAT may have a measurable financial return.


Always check the university's current scholarship page before assuming a score automatically qualifies you for an award. Scholarship thresholds and award amounts can change between admission cycles.


## What GPA Do You Need With a 1200 SAT?


There is no single GPA that “matches” a 1200 SAT score. Colleges evaluate GPA and SAT scores separately as parts of the broader academic profile.


A 1200 can be paired with a wide range of GPAs. What matters more is how your GPA compares with the typical academic profile at the colleges you're targeting.


A strong GPA with a 1200 may indicate that you perform well academically but have not maximized your standardized-test performance. In that situation, retaking the SAT could strengthen the application.


If your GPA is lower, a 1200 can provide additional evidence of academic preparation, although colleges will still consider your course rigor, grades, and academic trend.


## 1200 SAT Score: ACT Equivalent


A 1200 SAT is roughly equivalent to a 25 ACT composite, based on the standard concordance tables used by college counselors. Both scores sit in a similar percentile band.


Some students find one test format more natural than the other. The ACT includes a Science section and moves faster per question, while the digital SAT gives more time per question and uses an adaptive format. If your SAT section scores are notably uneven (say, 650 Reading & Writing and 550 Math), the ACT’s four-section structure might balance differently. Taking a diagnostic on both tests can reveal which plays to your strengths. If you’re curious about the ACT path, explore[ACT prep options](https://miyagilabs.ai/act/prep) to compare.


## Should You Retake the SAT After Scoring 1200?


A 1200 does not automatically mean you should retake the SAT. The best decision depends on your target colleges and what you want to achieve.


### Retake if:


-


Your target colleges commonly admit students with scores higher than 1200.


-


Your 1200 is below the 25th percentile at several target schools.


-


You are close to a scholarship score threshold.


-


Your practice tests consistently show that you can score meaningfully higher.


-


You have enough time to prepare without hurting your grades, applications, or other commitments.


### Consider stopping at 1200 if:


-


Your score is within or above the middle 50% range at most target schools.


-


You are satisfied with your college list.


-


Your target colleges are test-optional and your score does not strengthen your application.


-


Additional SAT preparation would take time away from stronger parts of your application.


### The simplest rule


If your 1200 is **below the 25th percentile at your target school, consider retaking** .


If it is **around the 50th percentile, it is generally competitive** .


If it is **above the 75th percentile, your score is unlikely to be the weakest part of your application** .


## Should You Submit a 1200 SAT Score? (Test-Optional Strategy)


Test-optional policies have changed the calculation. The rule of thumb: submit your score when it reinforces the story your transcript already tells.


**Submit when:**


-


Your 1200 is at or above the 25th percentile of admitted students at that school


-


Your GPA was affected by a temporary disruption but your SAT demonstrates academic readiness


-


You want to qualify for merit scholarships that require a test score


**Consider going test-optional when:**


-


The school’s middle-50% range starts well above 1200 (think UF, Georgia Tech, or any Ivy)


-


Your GPA and course rigor are strong enough to carry the application without a test score


One important nuance: test-optional policies have actually inflated the published score ranges at many schools, because students with lower scores simply don’t submit. The 25th-percentile number you see today is higher than it would be if everyone submitted. So a 1200 might be more competitive at a test-optional school than the published range suggests.


Purdue University, for example, explicitly advises students to submit if their SAT is 1200 or above.


## How to Improve From 1200 to 1300+ on the SAT


A 1200 to 1300 jump is very doable. It requires about 100 more points, which could come from one section alone. Here’s a practical roadmap.


**Start with a diagnostic.** Don’t just study “Math” or “Reading.” Identify the specific skill areas where you’re losing points. Maybe it’s algebra word problems or evidence-based reasoning questions. A targeted approach beats a generic one every time. Our[step-by-step improvement plan](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/how-to-improve-sat-score-by-200-points-5-step-plan) walks through this in detail.


**Focus on one section at a time.** If Math is your weaker section, a 50-point gain there moves you to 1250. Add 50 points on Reading & Writing and you’re at 1300. Small, section-specific gains compound.


**Use timed, full-length practice tests.** Stamina and pacing matter on test day. Taking a practice exam under real conditions reveals timing issues that section-only practice won’t surface. You can take[free SAT practice tests](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/practice-tests) to simulate the real experience.


**Drill weak skills with filtered practice.** Rather than working through random questions, use a[question bank](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/question-bank) that lets you filter by topic, skill, and difficulty. This is where targeted gains happen fastest.


**Track progress by section, not just total score.** Watch for plateaus in specific areas. If your Reading & Writing score stops climbing but Math is still rising, shift your focus.


**Aim for specific thresholds.** Don’t chase a vague “higher score.” If 1280 unlocks a scholarship at your top school, that’s your target. If 1350 puts you in the middle 50% at your dream school, plan around that number.


For a structured timeline, our[30-day SAT study plan](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/30-day-sat-study-plan) lays out exactly how to allocate your prep time.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is 1200 a good SAT score for Ivy League schools?


No. Ivy League schools (Harvard, Yale, Princeton, Columbia, Penn) admit students with scores almost exclusively above 1470, with most in the 1500+ range. A 1200 would be well below the 25th percentile at every Ivy League institution. You’d want to either significantly improve your score or go test-optional at these schools.


### Is 1200 a good SAT score for state schools?


Yes, for most state universities. Schools like Arizona State, Michigan State, Indiana University Bloomington, and the University of Oregon all have middle-50% ranges that include 1200. It makes you competitive at the majority of public universities in the country, though top public flagships like UF, Michigan, or UVA expect higher.


### What GPA pairs well with a 1200 SAT?


A GPA of 3.0 to 3.5+ generally aligns with a 1200 SAT in college admissions. If your GPA is significantly higher than what a 1200 would suggest, consider retaking to bring your test score in line with your transcript. If your GPA is lower, a 1200 can actually help demonstrate capability.


### How many questions can you miss and still get a 1200?


Roughly 20 to 25 questions across both sections, though the exact number varies by test form because of the digital SAT’s adaptive scoring. The first module’s performance determines the difficulty of the second module, which affects the scoring curve.


### Is 1200 good for a first attempt?


Absolutely. It’s well above average and gives you a strong foundation to build on. Most students improve on their second attempt, and a first-attempt 1200 suggests you could realistically reach 1300+ with focused preparation.


### Should I take the ACT instead if I scored 1200 on the SAT?


Not necessarily. A 1200 SAT is equivalent to about a 25 ACT, so switching tests doesn’t automatically give you an advantage. The decision should be based on which test format suits your strengths, not on escaping a score. Take a diagnostic for both and compare.


### Is 1200 enough for scholarships?


It’s the starting point. Several universities offer automatic merit awards at the 1200 threshold, including Alabama ($6,000/year with a 3.5+ GPA) and Oklahoma ($10,000/year). Pushing to 1300 or 1400 opens significantly larger awards at more schools.


### What percentile is a 1200 SAT score?


Among SAT test-takers, it’s approximately the 74th to 76th percentile. Among all U.S. students (nationally representative), it’s around the 81st percentile. Either way, you scored higher than the clear majority of students.


---


A 1200 is a good score that puts you in strong position for hundreds of colleges and the first tier of merit scholarships. Whether you stop here or push higher depends on your goals.
